A_Microstructure_OrderFlow_LOB.title: Corporate Leverage and Employees’ Rights in Bankruptcy Andrew Ellul
A_Microstructure_OrderFlow_LOB.abstract: Corporate leverage responds differently to employees’ rights in bankruptcy depending on whether it is driven by strategic concerns in wage bargaining or by credit constraints. Using novel data on employees’ rights in bankruptcy, we estimate their impact on leverage, exploiting time-series, cross-country and firm-level variation in the data. For financially unconstrained firms, results accord with the strategic debt model: leverage increases more in response to rises in corporate property values or profitability if employees have strong seniority in liquidation and weak rights in restructuring.

A_Microstructure_OrderFlow_LOB.abstract: We study intraday patterns of returns, trading activity, volatility and illiq- uidity in cryptocurrency markets. B_Liquidation_Toxicity_TailRisk.abstract: We examine the role of information flow in shaping volatility and tail risk of cryptocurrency returns. Using a stable-GJR-GARCH model with trading activity as a subordinator, we find that information flow increases conditional volatility while reducing—but not eliminating—heavy tails. Effects are stronger for more liquid cryptos. Trading days log-returns remain non-Gaussian even after correcting for information- induced heteroskedasticity within calendar days, challenging Gaussian assumptions in risk and asset-pricing models.

Specifically, a series of machine learning (ML) models are trained under various training settings (single- asset, cluster-driven, cross-asset, and pooled), where commonality progressively enters the model dynamics as training schemes become more complex. Our findings support the su- periority of models that leverage the cryptocurrency commonality over those that do not ex- plicitly account for it, regardless of market regimes.
